beginner.summary: For Python developers who are new to LlamaIndex and want to build retrieval-augmented generation applications over their own data. Covers installing llama-index-core and integration packages, the Settings object, Documents and Nodes, readers and SimpleDirectoryReader, node parsers and chunking, embeddings, VectorStoreIndex, persistence, retrievers, query engines and response modes, prompt templates, metadata filters, chat engines with memory, simple tools and function agents, first Workflows, and a document question-answering capstone.
prerequisites: Writes Python 3.10 or later with functions, classes, type hints, virtual environments and pip or uv
Can call a REST API with an API key held in an environment variable, and knows what an LLM prompt and an embedding are
Has an OpenAI-compatible API key or a local Ollama install, and a laptop with 8 GB of RAM and rights to install Python packages
outcomes: Install and configure LlamaIndex with a chosen LLM and embedding model and run a first query over local files
Load documents, split them into nodes with metadata, build and persist a VectorStoreIndex and reload it
Tune retrieval and response synthesis with top-k, filters, postprocessors and prompt templates, and read source nodes
Build a chat engine and a small function agent and deliver a cited document question-answering app with a recorded test set

intermediate.summary: For developers who have built a first LlamaIndex RAG app and now need it to be accurate, maintainable and measurable. Covers ingestion pipelines with caching, document management, Chroma and Qdrant vector stores, hybrid and fusion retrieval, metadata extractors, sentence-window and auto-merging retrieval, reranking, routers and sub-question engines, text-to-SQL, LlamaParse, retrieval evaluation with hit rate and MRR, synthetic test sets, multi-tool agents, branching and parallel Workflows, tracing with Arize Phoenix, async patterns, and a measured retrieval-improvement capstone.
prerequisites: Has built and queried a VectorStoreIndex with SimpleDirectoryReader, a custom prompt and a chat engine
Reads Python async code with async and await and uses pydantic models and pytest
Can run Docker locally to start Qdrant or Chroma, and has API keys for an LLM, an embedding model and optionally LlamaCloud
outcomes: Build an incremental ingestion pipeline with cache and docstore deduplication feeding a production vector store
Improve retrieval with hybrid search, fusion, sentence-window, auto-merging and reranking, and prove each gain with hit rate and MRR
Route and decompose questions across documents, SQL tables and tools with routers, sub-question engines and agents
Trace and test a multi-step Workflow with Phoenix and a regression test set

advanced.summary: For engineers who run LlamaIndex RAG and agent systems and need to extend, scale, secure and operate them. Covers property graph indexes and graph retrieval, agentic RAG with document agents, AgentWorkflow handoff, human-in-the-loop and resumable Workflows, reflection loops, MCP tools, multimodal RAG, LlamaExtract, LlamaCloud indexes, custom components, the instrumentation module, cost and latency control, regression gates in CI, tenant isolation, serving over FastAPI, failure diagnosis, and a production-grade agentic RAG capstone.
prerequisites: Has delivered a LlamaIndex RAG app with ingestion pipelines, reranking, evaluation and tracing
Writes async Python services with FastAPI, pydantic and pytest, and can read vector store and graph database documentation
Has access to a hosted or local LLM that supports tool calling, Docker for Neo4j or Qdrant, and optionally a LlamaCloud account
outcomes: Design graph, agentic and multi-agent retrieval systems with Workflows and AgentWorkflow and choose them only where they beat a plain pipeline
Extend LlamaIndex with custom retrievers, postprocessors, embeddings and instrumentation handlers
Control cost, latency, access and quality with caching, budgets, tenant filters and CI regression gates
Serve and troubleshoot a production RAG service with traces, metrics and a documented runbook
